user_query: Under which conditions would the node2vec sampling strategy that explores nodes at increasing distances be more consistent with DeepWalk's gains on Flickr and YouTube: when homophily dominates, or when structural equivalence matters more?
llm_response: When homophily dominates. DeepWalk’s gains on Flickr and YouTube are generally associated with capturing local neighborhood similarity, so a node2vec strategy that explores nodes at increasing distances would be more consistent with those gains in settings where nearby nodes tend to share labels or attributes rather than when structural equivalence is the main signal.
llm_confidence_reasoning: This aligns with the standard interpretation of DeepWalk/node2vec behavior on social-network benchmarks, though the exact phrasing depends on the specific experimental context.
